content.comment_body: A few years ago, I purchased a starter set for [product_name] [version_no], which included [product_name] software. I completed programming all my [product_name] devices without issues. Now, I have a new computer (MacBook Pro) and I'm facing difficulties installing the software. The system doesn't support PowerPC apps. I know that there are updates available for the software version, but I cannot get my basic version installed, which means I can't apply any updates or upgrades. Additionally, my Mac doesn't have a CD drive, making the installation CD unusable. Does anyone have a solution? Regards, [user_name]
The device likely has a USB port. Ask a friend to copy the CD contents to a USB stick for you.
That solution could work, but I'm unable to install an older version of the software. My system cannot run PowerPC applications.

You shouldn't try installing the old software. You can download the free upgrade from the [company_name] website at [url]. To install it, you'll need to reference an older full version, which could be placed on the USB stick.
@[user_name]: [user_name] suggested a good approach. The following instructions are for Windows users but may also be helpful for you. Check if anything from [url] is useful.
Hello [user_name], thanks for the comprehensive advice.
This is excellent! I really appreciate your help, and it worked perfectly. Thank you!

analysis.insight_summary: The user ran into a compatibility issue with installing [product_name] software (part of a [product_name] [version_no] starter set) on a recent MacBook Pro, since the original installer required PowerPC architecture and a CD drive, both unsupported by the current hardware and operating system. This prevented installation of the base software, and thus blocked applying updates and upgrades. The absence of a CD drive added to the complexity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to easily install and update their [company_name] software on modern Mac computers and operating systems, independent of hardware features like CD drives or support for legacy architectures.
